241af42a6a.q: What health symptoms did Christine Furumoto experience from work-related stress at San Diego PD before creating SweatJoy?
241af42a6a.a: When she left San Diego PD, her skin was peeling off her fingertips so severely she could no longer be fingerprinted, her hair was falling out, and she was holding her breath constantly. She eventually became so exhausted she was hospitalized and experienced a complete shutdown, which forced her to prioritize her own needs and led to developing the SweatJoy app.
241af42a6a.e: 360: Crisis and Dispatch Work Takes a Toll, What Are We Doing to Help Our Teams?
241af42a6a.rq: I had been denying what my needs are for so many years that I don't know why capable people do this. When you're denying your physical body, it talks to you and your nervous system is going to shout out.

7075de8c82.q: What is SweatJoy and what features does it offer for first responders?
7075de8c82.a: SweatJoy is an app that offers mindfulness, movement, nutrition, and community for first responders. It includes a resource directory with licensed clinicians experienced in first responder trauma, and allows users to monitor their water intake, breathing, mood, and connect with other first responders in a supportive community while working independently on their wellness.

8a18e80ad3.q: How long does it take for new dispatchers in large cities like San Diego to feel comfortable in their role?
8a18e80ad3.a: According to Christine Furumoto, it takes about a year to really get used to the dispatcher job, at least in a big city like San Diego. She emphasized not being hard on yourself during this adjustment period and recommended having support from other dispatchers and learning to breathe and manage your nervous system.

c23940ca5c.q: What micro-habits does Christine Furumoto recommend for dispatch and crisis response workers to manage stress?
c23940ca5c.a: She recommends simple micro-habits including proper breathing exercises, staying hydrated, movement activities or physical exercise, monitoring your nervous system state, using sit-stand desks when available, and taking breaks to release tension—such as brief treadmill sessions. She emphasizes that these free, basic practices create huge change over time and prevent stress accumulation.

0b11f12218.q: What did Christine Furumoto learn from her crisis line work that prepared her for dispatch?
0b11f12218.a: She learned to have an ear and listen without telling people what to do, but instead show them a different way of seeing their situation and a different outcome. She learned to adapt to different personalities on the phone, listen between the words, and decipher tones and pitches to extract accurate information for responding units.
